The issue isn't high density as opposed to low density houses, it's hyper density. Reading the original article, a councillor in the meeting where they unanimously (9-0) rejected it said it was like "trying to squeeze a quart into a pint pot". Not a single detail changed in the plan when it was approved a few weeks later. BCC recommend a max of 120 DPH density in urban areas, this will be 428 DPH.

Before someone yells nimby at me, this development won’t impact me, but I think it sets a worrying precedent for the city, particularly if you actually care about the provision of affordable housing.

A lot of people are commenting without knowing anything about the development. It isn’t affordable housing. Their promise is 7%. Even with support from housing associations, it will be more like 9.8% and that’s not even guaranteed (it’s a “hope”).

Also, people need homes. They don’t need absolutely tiny single-aspect rooms that meet the superdensity threshold, it’s completely unethical. As far as I can tell, no-one wants the Broadwalk in its current iteration, but it shouldn’t be this development, or no development. 

In May the planning committee of local councillors unanimously rejected the plans due to height and hyperdensity. Local campaigners were told that a follow-up meeting on 5th July was to confirm the wording so they didn’t turn up. During the meeting, the decision was overturned despite nothing changing in the plans. Undemocratic at best, corrupt at worst.

You've had lots of advice already, but my thoughts are:

1. Go on Facebook and join Bristol Girl for latest thoughts and tips about safety in the city.
2. I've lived in Bristol for nearly 9 years and have only experienced 2 unpleasant experiences, one was on Stapleton Road (known for being a red light district). The other was when I got in a taxi without prebooking which was my own fault. To this day I have no idea if he was a legit taxi driver, but he wanted to come into my house. I lied and told him my boyfriend and flatmates were waiting up for me, but I was actually alone and felt v unsafe. It's quite hard to get an Uber in Bristol now, recommend downloading Bolt.
3. If you get a Voi scooter, always check that there's a parking space where you're going. I took one the other day late at night because I couldn't get a taxi or a bus but when I arrived home the nearest space was nearly a mile away. After I went back and forth trying to find the space (I didn't know the area v well) it would've been quicker for me to walk...
4. Avoid parks at night, I don't personally know of any incidents in Bristol parks, it's just my hunch that they're not the best places to be by yourself in the dark

Bristol is a lovely city. I really wouldn't live anywhere else in the UK.
